newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Gevaert sees '97 result in line with '96.
newsitem.headline: Gevaert sees '97 result in line with '96.

text.p: Belgian holding company Gevaert NV told shareholders on Thursday it expected 1997 results to be in line with those of 1996.

"With regard to the outlook for 1997 it can be expected that, based on dividend income and the capital gains forecast for this financial year -- with current market conditions presumed to persist -- the group's results will be in line with 1996 results," chairman Andre Leysen told the annual meeting, according to a text released by the company.
Gevaert consolidated net earnings rose to 4.23 billion Belgian francs in 1996 from 2.94 billion in 1995. Current income rose to 2.22 billion francs from 1.89 billion.

Leysen put the net asset value per share on April 15 "taking into account the estimated profit for the first quarter of 1997 and before payment of the dividend over 1996" at 3,152 francs compared with a market price of 2,540 francs.
Gevaert plans to pay 1996 net dividend of 55 francs a share, up 10 percent on 1995.
